Title: SOP Number
Content: SOP-QA-014

Title: Effective Date
Content: March 1, 2026

Title: Review Cycle
Content: Annual

Title: Document Owner
Content: Quality Assurance Dept.

Title: Approved By
Content: Plant Quality Manager

Title: Applicable Site(s)
Content: Line 3 / Line 4 (Shared)

Title: Classification
Content: Internal - Controlled

Title: Purpose
Content: Defines required steps for cleaning, sanitizing, and verifying shared production lines between production runs involving different major food allergens; reduces risk of undeclared allergen cross-contact and provides a documented basis for line release decisions.

Title: Scope
Content: Applies to all changeovers on Line 3 and Line 4 where a run with one or more major allergens is followed by a run with a different allergen profile, including allergen-free products. Covers dry clean-up, wet cleaning (CIP/COP), sanitization, and post-sanitation verification. Does not cover general equipment maintenance (see SOP-ME-002).

Title: Major Food Allergen
Content: One of the nine allergens recognized under U.S. labeling law: milk, eggs, fish, crustacean shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, soybeans, and sesame.

Title: Allergen Changeover
Content: A cleaning and verification event that occurs specifically because the upcoming run has a different allergen profile than the preceding run.

Title: CIP (Clean-in-Place)
Content: Automated circulation of cleaning and sanitizing solutions through enclosed process equipment without disassembly.

Title: COP (Clean-out-of-Place)
Content: Manual removal, disassembly, and cleaning of parts outside the line, typically in a dedicated wash sink or parts washer.

Title: ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) Swab
Content: A rapid bioluminescence test used to verify general cleanliness of a surface, reported in Relative Light Units (RLU).

Title: Validated Cleaning
Content: A cleaning method documented, through allergen-specific testing, to reliably reduce allergen residue below the site action limit.

Title: Line Operator
Content: Performs pre-cleaning teardown, removes gross soil, and completes the Line Clearance Checklist prior to handoff to Sanitation.

Title: Sanitation Technician
Content: Executes the wet-clean (CIP/COP) cycle, verifies chemical concentrations, and records contact times on the Sanitation Log.

Title: QA Technician
Content: Performs post-sanitation ATP swabbing and allergen surface testing; approves or rejects the line for allergen changeover release.

Title: Shift Supervisor
Content: Confirms changeover schedule, resolves scheduling conflicts between allergen runs, and co-signs the Line Release Form.

Title: Plant Quality Manager
Content: Owns this SOP, reviews deviation reports, and approves any temporary variance to stated parameters.

Title: Alkaline CIP detergent
Content: 1.5% to 2.0% w/v working solution

Title: Acid rinse additive
Content: 0.5% w/v working solution, used on lines processing dairy soils

Title: Peracetic-acid-based sanitizer
Content: 150-200 ppm working concentration

Title: ATP luminometer and single-use swabs
Content: Calibrated per manufacturer schedule

Title: Allergen-specific lateral flow or ELISA test kits
Content: Allergen-dependent; see Attachment B

Title: Color-coded cleaning tools
Content: Dedicated by allergen zone per SOP-QA-009

Title: Step 1
Content: Line Operator confirms the production schedule and identifies the allergen status of the completed run and the upcoming run.

Title: Step 2
Content: Remove all in-process product, packaging, and labels from the line; segregate for disposition per SOP-QA-011.

Title: Step 3
Content: Complete the Line Clearance Checklist and route to the Shift Supervisor for initial sign-off.

Title: Step 4
Content: Disconnect and stage disassembled parts for COP cleaning in the designated wash area.

Title: Step 5
Content: Remove gross soil, product residue, and loose debris using dedicated dry tools (brushes, scrapers, vacuum).

Title: Step 6
Content: Do not introduce water at this stage; wet debris is significantly harder to fully remove during CIP and increases allergen carryover risk.

Title: Step 7
Content: Dispose of collected debris in allergen-labeled waste receptacles.

Title: Step 8
Content: Circulate a pre-rinse of potable water to remove residual soil.

Title: Step 9
Content: Circulate alkaline detergent solution.

Title: Step 10
Content: For lines with heavy dairy or protein soiling, follow with an acid rinse additive.

Title: Step 11
Content: Intermediate rinse with potable water until effluent runs clear and pH is within range.

Title: Step 12
Content: For COP items, submerge in the same detergent concentration with manual agitation, then rinse.

Title: Step 13
Content: QA Technician reviews the changeover matrix in Attachment B to confirm whether the CIP/COP cycle constitutes Validated Cleaning for the allergen pair involved.

Title: Step 14
Content: If the changeover matrix indicates a non-validated pair, perform a second full detergent cycle (repeat step 6.3, items 2-4) before proceeding.

Title: Step 15
Content: Visually inspect all product contact surfaces, gaskets, and dead-leg areas using a flashlight; document any residue found on the Visual Inspection Log.

Title: Step 16
Content: Do not proceed to sanitization until visual inspection is passed and documented.

Title: Step 17
Content: Circulate peracetic-acid-based sanitizer on all product contact surfaces.

Title: Step 18
Content: Verify concentration using a test strip or titration prior to circulation; record the reading on the Sanitation Log.

Title: Step 19
Content: Allow product contact surfaces to air dry; do not towel-dry with non-dedicated cloths.

Title: Step 20
Content: QA Technician swabs a minimum of five predetermined product contact points using the ATP luminometer.

Title: Step 21
Content: A reading below threshold at each point is required to pass; at or above threshold requires re-cleaning and re-swabbing before the line may proceed.

Title: Step 22
Content: For allergen changeovers identified as non-validated in step 13, QA Technician additionally performs allergen-specific surface testing per Attachment B; a result below the site action limit is required to release the line.

Title: Step 23
Content: QA Technician completes and signs the Line Release Form; Shift Supervisor co-signs before production may resume.

Title: Re-clean on failure
Content: The affected surface or the full line (QA Technician's determination, based on failure pattern) is re-cleaned per Section 6.3 before re-testing.

Title: Two consecutive failures
Content: Two consecutive failures at the same point trigger a documented deviation report and notification to the Plant Quality Manager before a third attempt.

Title: Product hold
Content: Any product run before a passing verification result is documented is placed on hold pending disposition review.

Title: Repeated failures
Content: Repeated failures (3 or more events in a rolling 30-day period) on the same line trigger a root-cause investigation per SOP-QA-020.

Title: Record Retention
Content: Line Clearance Checklist, Sanitation Log, Visual Inspection Log, ATP and allergen test results, Line Release Form, and deviation reports retained by QA Department.

Title: Training Requirements
Content: Initial allergen awareness and sanitation training with demonstrated competency required before working unsupervised. Refresher training required annually and whenever a stated parameter (concentration, time, or temperature) changes.
